subject: math
title: Grade 8 Pythagorean Theorem
seo_title: Grade 8 Pythagorean Theorem Worksheets: Free Math Practice with Answer Key (BC Curriculum)
meta_desc: Free Grade 8 math worksheets on the Pythagorean theorem for the BC curriculum: squares on the sides, finding the hypotenuse or a missing leg (to the nearest tenth), checking for a right triangle, and ladder, ramp and field problems. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_sub: In a right triangle, the square on the hypotenuse c (opposite the right angle) equals the squares on the two legs added. Square the sides first, then add or subtract, then take the square root.
body_html:
Legs and hypotenuse

A right triangle has one 90° angle, shown with a small square. The two sides that form the right angle are the legs (a and b). The side opposite the right angle is the hypotenuse (c). It is always the longest side, and it can point in any direction.

The area model: a² + b² = c²

Draw a square on each side of a right triangle. The two squares on the legs together have exactly the same area as the square on the hypotenuse. This is the Pythagorean theorem.

It only works for right triangles. It also works the other way: if a² + b² = c², the triangle has a right angle.

Find the hypotenuse: add the squares

Square the two legs, add, then take the square root.

Example

The legs are 6 cm and 8 cm. Find the hypotenuse.

c² = 6² + 8² = 36 + 64 = 100. c = √100 = 10.

Answer: 10 cm

Round at the end

The legs are 4 cm and 7 cm. Find the hypotenuse to the nearest tenth.

c² = 16 + 49 = 65. c = √65 ≈ 8.06, which rounds to 8.1.

Answer: 8.1 cm

Find a leg: subtract the squares

Square the hypotenuse and the known leg, subtract, then take the square root.

A leg is always shorter than the hypotenuse. If your answer is longer, you added instead of subtracting.

Is it a right triangle? Check the squares

You cannot tell a right angle just by looking. Square the two shorter sides and add. If the sum equals the square of the longest side, the triangle has a right angle.

Right triangle

A triangle has sides of 9 cm, 12 cm and 15 cm. Is it a right triangle?

9² + 12² = 81 + 144 = 225, and 15² = 225. They are equal.

Answer: Yes, it is a right triangle.

Not a right triangle

A triangle has sides of 7 cm, 8 cm and 11 cm. Is it a right triangle?

7² + 8² = 49 + 64 = 113, but 11² = 121. They are not equal.

Answer: No (113 ≠ 121).

Pythagorean triples

Some right triangles have three whole-number sides. Multiples of a triple are triples too (6, 8, 10).

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Adding the sides without squaring: 3 + 4 = 7Square first: 3² + 4² = 25, so c = 5
Subtracting to find the hypotenuseHypotenuse: add the squares. Leg: subtract
Stopping at c² = 25Take the square root: c = 5
Calling the bottom side the hypotenuseFind the side opposite the right angle
Checking with the last number listedAlways use the longest side as c
Rounding before the last stepRound only the final square root

faq.q: Is the Pythagorean theorem in the BC Grade 8 math curriculum?
faq.a: Yes. The Pythagorean theorem is a Grade 8 content standard in Geometry and measurement in the BC math curriculum. Students model it with squares on the sides of a right triangle and use it to find missing side lengths.

faq.q: How do you know which side is the hypotenuse?
faq.a: The hypotenuse is the side opposite the right angle, and it is always the longest side. The two sides that form the right angle are the legs.

faq.q: How do you find a missing leg with the Pythagorean theorem?
faq.a: Subtract instead of add: square the hypotenuse and the known leg, subtract, then take the square root. For example, √(13² − 5²) = √144 = 12.

faq.q: How can you tell if a triangle is a right triangle from its sides?
faq.a: Square the two shorter sides and add them. If the total equals the square of the longest side, as in 6, 8 and 10 (36 + 64 = 100), it is a right triangle; if not, it is not.

sets.title: Squares on the sides: the area model

items.q: Squares are drawn on the sides of a right triangle. What is the area of the square on the hypotenuse?
items.e: The square on the hypotenuse equals the two smaller squares put together: 40 + 24 = 64 m². (The hypotenuse itself is √64 = 8 m long.)

items.q: Squares are drawn on the sides of a right triangle. What is the area of the square marked “?”
items.e: The two squares on the legs add up to the square on the hypotenuse: ? + 16 = 41. So ? = 41 − 16 = 25 cm².

items.q: The squares on the legs of a right triangle have areas of 36 m² and 64 m². How long is the hypotenuse?
items.e: The square on the hypotenuse is 36 + 64 = 100 m². Its side is √100 = 10 m.

items.q: Each choice gives the areas of three squares, in cm². Which three squares could be drawn on the sides of a right triangle?
items.e: The two smaller areas must add up to the largest: 64 + 225 = 289. Check the others: 8 + 15 = 23, not 17; 64 + 225 = 289, not 256; 49 + 64 = 113, not 121.

items.q: Each choice gives the areas of three squares, in cm². Which three squares could be drawn on the sides of a right triangle?
items.e: The two smaller areas must add up to the largest: 25 + 144 = 169. Check the others: 25 + 144 = 169, not 196; 5 + 12 = 17, not 13; 16 + 25 = 41, not 36.

items.q: Which statement about the squares on the sides of a right triangle is always true?
c: The square on a leg is the largest.
The square on the bottom side is the largest.
All three squares are the same size.
The square on the hypotenuse is the largest.
items.e: The square on the hypotenuse (the side opposite the right angle) is the largest square. It equals the two squares on the legs added together.

items.q: A right triangle has a hypotenuse of 17 cm and one leg of 8 cm. What is the area of the square on the other leg?
items.e: Square on the hypotenuse: 17² = 289 cm². Square on the known leg: 8² = 64 cm². Other square: 289 − 64 = 225 cm².

items.q: The legs of a right triangle are 5 cm and 12 cm. What is the area of the square on the hypotenuse?

items.q: The square on the hypotenuse of a right triangle has an area of 169 cm². How long is the hypotenuse?
items.e: The side of a square is the square root of its area: √169 = 13 cm, because 13 × 13 = 169.

items.q: Which equation is true for this right triangle?
items.e: The hypotenuse is r, the side opposite the right angle (here it lies along the bottom). The squares on the legs add up to the square on the hypotenuse: p² + q² = r².

sets.title: Is it a right triangle? (the converse)

items.q: Which triangle is NOT a right triangle?
items.e: Check each one. 5² + 7² = 25 + 49 = 74, but 9² = 81, so 5, 7 and 9 is not a right triangle. The others work: 9 + 16 = 25, 25 + 144 = 169 and 36 + 64 = 100.

items.q: A triangle has sides of 7 cm, 8 cm and 11 cm. Is it a right triangle?
c: Yes: 11 cm is the longest side
items.e: Square the two shorter sides and add: 7² + 8² = 49 + 64 = 113. Square the longest side: 11² = 121. 113 ≠ 121, so it is not a right triangle. (The largest angle is a little more than 90°.)

items.q: A triangle has sides of 13 cm, 5 cm and 12 cm. Is it a right triangle?
items.e: Square the two shorter sides and add: 5² + 12² = 25 + 144 = 169. Square the longest side: 13² = 169. They are equal, so it is a right triangle. The right angle is opposite the 13 cm side. Always use the longest side as the hypotenuse, even when it is not listed last.

items.q: The side lengths of this triangle are shown. Is it a right triangle?
c: Yes: 21 mm is the longest side
items.e: Square the two shorter sides and add: 12² + 16² = 144 + 256 = 400. Square the longest side: 21² = 441. 400 ≠ 441, so it is not a right triangle. (The largest angle is a little more than 90°.)

items.q: The side lengths of this triangle are shown. Is it a right triangle?
c: Yes: 17 cm is the longest side
items.e: Square the two shorter sides and add: 11² + 13² = 121 + 169 = 290. Square the longest side: 17² = 289. 290 ≠ 289, so it is not a right triangle. (The largest angle is a little less than 90°.)

items.q: A triangle has sides of 6 cm, 8 cm and 10 cm. Is it a right triangle?
items.e: Square the two shorter sides and add: 6² + 8² = 36 + 64 = 100. Square the longest side: 10² = 100. They are equal, so it is a right triangle. The right angle is opposite the 10 cm side.

items.q: A triangle has sides of 1.5 m, 2 m and 2.5 m. Is it a right triangle?
items.e: Square the two shorter sides and add: 1.5² + 2² = 2.25 + 4 = 6.25. Square the longest side: 2.5² = 6.25. They are equal, so it is a right triangle. The right angle is opposite the 2.5 m side.

items.q: A triangle has sides of 7 m and 24 m. How long must the longest side be for the triangle to have a right angle?
items.e: The longest side is the hypotenuse: √(7² + 24²) = √(49 + 576) = √625 = 25 m.

items.q: Which three side lengths make a right triangle?
items.e: Check that the squares of the two shorter sides add up to the square of the longest side: 0.9² + 1.2² = 0.81 + 1.44 = 2.25 = 1.5². In the other choices the squares do not match.

items.q: A triangle has sides of 16 cm and 30 cm. How long must the longest side be for the triangle to have a right angle?
items.e: The longest side is the hypotenuse: √(16² + 30²) = √(256 + 900) = √1156 = 34 cm.

items.q: The side lengths of this triangle are shown. Is it a right triangle?
items.e: Square the two shorter sides and add: 20² + 21² = 400 + 441 = 841. Square the longest side: 29² = 841. They are equal, so it is a right triangle. The right angle is opposite the 29 mm side.

items.q: A triangle has sides of 9 m, 10 m and 14 m. Is it a right triangle?
c: Yes: 14 m is the longest side
items.e: Square the two shorter sides and add: 9² + 10² = 81 + 100 = 181. Square the longest side: 14² = 196. 181 ≠ 196, so it is not a right triangle. (The largest angle is a little more than 90°.)

items.q: Which three side lengths make a right triangle?
items.e: Check that the squares of the two shorter sides add up to the square of the longest side: 12² + 35² = 144 + 1225 = 1369 = 37². In the other choices the squares do not match.

items.q: A triangle has sides of 9 cm, 12 cm and 15 cm. Is it a right triangle?
items.e: Square the two shorter sides and add: 9² + 12² = 81 + 144 = 225. Square the longest side: 15² = 225. They are equal, so it is a right triangle. The right angle is opposite the 15 cm side.

items.q: Which three side lengths make a right triangle?
items.e: Check that the squares of the two shorter sides add up to the square of the longest side: 9² + 40² = 81 + 1600 = 1681 = 41². In the other choices the squares do not match.

items.q: Owen builds a raised garden bed. To check a corner, he marks 60 cm along one side and 80 cm along the other. The distance between the marks is 100 cm. Is the corner a right angle?
items.e: 60² + 80² = 3600 + 6400 = 10 000 = 100². The sides fit a² + b² = c², so the corner is a right angle.

items.q: 3, 4 and 5 is a Pythagorean triple. Which of these is also a Pythagorean triple?
items.e: Multiply every number in a triple by the same number and you get another triple: 3 × 5 = 15, 4 × 5 = 20, 5 × 5 = 25. Check: 225 + 400 = 625 = 25². Adding the same number to each side does not work: 4, 5, 6 gives 16 + 25 = 41, not 36.

items.q: A triangle has sides of 24 cm, 10 cm and 25 cm. Is it a right triangle?
c: Yes: 25 cm is the longest side
items.e: Square the two shorter sides and add: 10² + 24² = 100 + 576 = 676. Square the longest side: 25² = 625. 676 ≠ 625, so it is not a right triangle. (The largest angle is a little less than 90°.)

items.q: A triangle has sides of 4 m, 6 m and 7 m. Is it a right triangle?
c: Yes: 7 m is the longest side
items.e: Square the two shorter sides and add: 4² + 6² = 16 + 36 = 52. Square the longest side: 7² = 49. 52 ≠ 49, so it is not a right triangle. (The largest angle is a little less than 90°.)

items.q: Nadia checks a corner of a deck frame the same way: 60 cm along one side, 80 cm along the other, and she measures 96 cm between the marks. What can she conclude?
items.e: For a right angle the distance would be √(60² + 80²) = √10 000 = 100 cm. 96 cm is shorter, so the two sides are pulled closer together: the corner is less than 90°.

sets.title: Word problems: ladders, ramps and diagonals across fields

items.q: To clean the gutters, Kai leans a ladder against the house so that it reaches 4.8 m up the wall. The foot of the ladder is 1.4 m from the wall. How long is the ladder?
items.e: c² = 4.8² + 1.4² = 23.04 + 1.96 = 25. c = √25 = 5 m. The ladder is opposite the right angle between the wall and the ground.

A firefighter in Kamloops needs a ladder to reach a window 6 m above the ground. For safety, the foot of the ladder must be 1.5 m from the wall. How long must the ladder be? Round to the nearest tenth.
A garden gate is 1.2 m wide and 1 m tall. A wooden brace goes from one corner to the opposite corner. How long is the brace? Round to the nearest tenth.

items.e: h² = 50² − 30² = 2500 − 900 = 1600. h = √1600 = 40 m. The string is the hypotenuse.

items.q: A playing field in Burnaby is a rectangle 120 m long and 50 m wide. A path goes straight across it from one corner to the opposite corner. How long is the path?
The bases on a baseball diamond form a square with sides of 27.4 m. How far does the catcher throw from home plate straight to second base? Round to the nearest tenth.
items.e: c² = 27.4² + 27.4² = 750.76 + 750.76 = 1501.52. c = √1501.52 ≈ 38.74…, which rounds to 38.7 m. Home plate, first base and second base make a right triangle.

items.q: A 3 m ramp goes from the back of a moving truck to the ground. The back of the truck is 0.9 m high. How far from the truck does the ramp touch the ground? Round to the nearest tenth.
items.e: d² = 3² − 0.9² = 9 − 0.81 = 8.19. d = √8.19 ≈ 2.86…, which rounds to 2.9 m. The ramp is the hypotenuse.

items.q: A wheelchair ramp at a community centre in Surrey rises 0.5 m over a horizontal distance of 6 m. How long is the sloping surface of the ramp? Round to the nearest tenth.
A square community garden in Nanaimo is 40 m on each side. How long is a path straight across it from one corner to the opposite corner? Round to the nearest tenth.
A 6 m ladder leans against the wall of Ava’s family cabin on Vancouver Island. Its foot is 1.5 m from the wall. How high up the wall does the ladder reach? Round to the nearest tenth.
items.e: h² = 6² − 1.5² = 36 − 2.25 = 33.75. h = √33.75 ≈ 5.80…, which rounds to 5.8 m. The ladder is the hypotenuse; the ground and the wall are the legs.
